normative.quote: Numbers here are in the Ethernet standard, which is high byte first.
normative.obligation: An implementation must encode numeric fields of the packet high byte first, in the Ethernet standard byte order.

normative.quote: Therefore, special care must be taken with the opcode field (ar$op) described below.
normative.obligation: An implementation must take special care that the opcode field ar$op is emitted and read in high-byte-first order rather than in the host's native byte order.

normative.quote: However, the 10Mbit Ethernet requires 48.bit addresses on the physical cable, yet most protocol addresses are not 48.bits long
normative.obligation: An implementation relies on 10Mbit Ethernet hardware addresses being 48 bits wide on the cable, and must not assume a protocol address has the same length as or any relationship to that Ethernet address.

normative.quote: ares_op$REQUEST (= 1, high byte transmitted first)
normative.obligation: An implementation must use the value 1 for the request opcode ares_op$REQUEST.

normative.quote: ares_op$REPLY   (= 2)
normative.obligation: An implementation must use the value 2 for the reply opcode ares_op$REPLY.

normative.quote: ares_hrd$Ethernet (= 1)
normative.obligation: An implementation must use the value 1 for the Ethernet hardware address space ares_hrd$Ethernet.

normative.quote: To communicate mappings from <protocol, address> pairs to 48.bit Ethernet addresses, a packet format that embodies the Address Resolution protocol is needed.
normative.obligation: An implementation must communicate <protocol, address> to 48-bit Ethernet address mappings using the packet format given below, not a format of its own choosing.

normative.quote: 48.bit: Ethernet address of destination
normative.obligation: The Ethernet transmission layer of the packet begins with a 48-bit destination Ethernet address.

normative.quote: 48.bit: Ethernet address of sender
normative.obligation: The 48-bit Ethernet address of the sender follows the destination address in the Ethernet transmission layer of the packet.

normative.quote: 16.bit: Protocol type = ether_type$ADDRESS_RESOLUTION
normative.obligation: The 16-bit Ethernet protocol type field of an address resolution packet must hold ether_type$ADDRESS_RESOLUTION.

normative.quote: 16.bit: (ar$hrd) Hardware address space (e.g., Ethernet, Packet Radio Net.)
normative.obligation: The packet data begins with a 16-bit ar$hrd field naming the hardware address space.

normative.quote: 16.bit: (ar$pro) Protocol address space.  For Ethernet hardware, this is from the set of type fields ether_typ$<protocol>.
normative.obligation: A 16-bit ar$pro field naming the protocol address space follows ar$hrd, and for Ethernet hardware its value is drawn from the ether_type$ set.

normative.quote: 8.bit: (ar$hln) byte length of each hardware address
normative.obligation: An 8-bit ar$hln field giving the byte length of each hardware address follows ar$pro.

normative.quote: 8.bit: (ar$pln) byte length of each protocol address
normative.obligation: An 8-bit ar$pln field giving the byte length of each protocol address follows ar$hln.

normative.quote: 16.bit: (ar$op)  opcode (ares_op$REQUEST | ares_op$REPLY)
normative.obligation: A 16-bit ar$op opcode field follows ar$pln and carries either ares_op$REQUEST or ares_op$REPLY.

normative.quote: nbytes: (ar$sha) Hardware address of sender of this packet, n from the ar$hln field.
normative.obligation: An ar$sha field holding the sender's hardware address follows ar$op, and its length in bytes is the value of ar$hln.

normative.quote: mbytes: (ar$spa) Protocol address of sender of this packet, m from the ar$pln field.
normative.obligation: An ar$spa field holding the sender's protocol address follows ar$sha, and its length in bytes is the value of ar$pln.

normative.quote: nbytes: (ar$tha) Hardware address of target of this packet (if known).
normative.obligation: An ar$tha field holding the target's hardware address, if known, follows ar$spa, and its length in bytes is the value of ar$hln.

normative.quote: mbytes: (ar$tpa) Protocol address of target.
normative.obligation: An ar$tpa field holding the target's protocol address follows ar$tha, and its length in bytes is the value of ar$pln.

normative.quote: In the case of the 10Mbit Ethernet, address resolution is needed and some lower layer (probably the hardware driver) must consult the Address Resolution module (perhaps implemented in the Ethernet support module) to convert the <protocol type, target protocol address> pair to a 48.bit Ethernet address.
normative.obligation: Before transmitting on 10Mbit Ethernet, the lower layer must consult the Address Resolution module to convert the <protocol type, target protocol address> pair into a 48-bit Ethernet address.

normative.quote: The Address Resolution module tries to find this pair in a table.
normative.obligation: On being consulted, the Address Resolution module must look the <protocol type, target protocol address> pair up in its translation table.

normative.quote: If it finds the pair, it gives the corresponding 48.bit Ethernet address back to the caller (hardware driver) which then transmits the packet.
normative.obligation: If the lookup finds the pair, the module must return the corresponding 48-bit Ethernet address to the calling hardware driver, which then transmits the packet.

normative.quote: If it does not, it probably informs the caller that it is throwing the packet away
normative.obligation: If the lookup fails, the module probably informs the caller that the outbound packet is being discarded.

normative.quote: it is throwing the packet away (on the assumption the packet will be retransmitted by a higher network layer)
normative.obligation: If the lookup fails, the module must discard the outbound packet rather than queue or transmit it, relying on a higher network layer to retransmit.

normative.quote: generates an Ethernet packet with a type field of ether_type$ADDRESS_RESOLUTION
normative.obligation: After a failed lookup the module must generate an Ethernet packet whose type field is ether_type$ADDRESS_RESOLUTION.

normative.quote: The Address Resolution module then sets the ar$hrd field to ares_hrd$Ethernet
normative.obligation: In a generated request the module must set ar$hrd to ares_hrd$Ethernet.

normative.quote: ar$pro to the protocol type that is being resolved
normative.obligation: In a generated request the module must set ar$pro to the protocol type whose address is being resolved.

normative.quote: ar$hln to 6 (the number of bytes in a 48.bit Ethernet address)
normative.obligation: In a generated request on Ethernet the module must set ar$hln to 6.

normative.quote: ar$pln to the length of an address in that protocol
normative.obligation: In a generated request the module must set ar$pln to the byte length of an address in the protocol being resolved.

normative.quote: ar$op to ares_op$REQUEST
normative.obligation: In a generated request the module must set ar$op to ares_op$REQUEST.

normative.quote: ar$sha with the 48.bit ethernet address of itself
normative.obligation: In a generated request the module must set ar$sha to its own 48-bit Ethernet address.

normative.quote: ar$spa with the protocol address of itself
normative.obligation: In a generated request the module must set ar$spa to its own protocol address.

normative.quote: ar$tpa with the protocol address of the machine that is trying to be accessed
normative.obligation: In a generated request the module must set ar$tpa to the protocol address of the machine being accessed.

normative.quote: It does not set ar$tha to anything in particular, because it is this value that it is trying to determine.
normative.obligation: In a generated request ar$tha is left unconstrained, so an implementation need not set it to any particular value and a peer must not rely on its contents.

normative.quote: It could set ar$tha to the broadcast address for the hardware (all ones in the case of the 10Mbit Ethernet) if that makes it convenient for some aspect of the implementation.
normative.obligation: An implementation is permitted ("could") to set ar$tha in a generated request to the hardware broadcast address, all ones on 10Mbit Ethernet, if that is convenient.

normative.quote: It then causes this packet to be broadcast to all stations on the Ethernet cable originally determined by the routing mechanism.
normative.obligation: The module must broadcast the generated request to all stations on the cable that routing selected for the original packet.

normative.quote: When an address resolution packet is received, the receiving Ethernet module gives the packet to the Address Resolution module
normative.obligation: On receipt of an address resolution packet the Ethernet module must hand the packet to the Address Resolution module for processing.

normative.quote: Negative conditionals indicate an end of processing and a discarding of the packet.
normative.obligation: Whenever a conditional test in the reception algorithm fails, the implementation must end processing and discard the received packet.

normative.quote: ?Do I have the hardware type in ar$hrd?
normative.obligation: The receiver must first test whether it implements the hardware type named in ar$hrd, and proceed only if it does.

normative.quote: [optionally check the hardware length ar$hln]
normative.obligation: The receiver may optionally check the hardware address length ar$hln, and may skip that check.

normative.quote: ?Do I speak the protocol in ar$pro?
normative.obligation: The receiver must test whether it speaks the protocol named in ar$pro, and proceed only if it does.

normative.quote: [optionally check the protocol length ar$pln]
normative.obligation: The receiver may optionally check the protocol address length ar$pln, and may skip that check.

normative.quote: Merge_flag := false
normative.obligation: The receiver must initialise Merge_flag to false before examining the translation table.

normative.quote: If the pair <protocol type, sender protocol address> is already in my translation table, update the sender hardware address field of the entry with the new information in the packet
normative.obligation: If the <protocol type, sender protocol address> pair is already in the translation table, the receiver must update that entry's hardware address with the sender hardware address from the packet.

normative.quote: set Merge_flag to true
normative.obligation: When an existing entry is updated, the receiver must set Merge_flag to true.

normative.quote: ?Am I the target protocol address?
normative.obligation: After the merge step the receiver must test whether ar$tpa is its own protocol address, and proceed only if it is.

normative.quote: If Merge_flag is false, add the triplet <protocol type, sender protocol address, sender hardware address> to the translation table.
normative.obligation: If the receiver is the target and Merge_flag is false, it must add the triplet <protocol type, sender protocol address, sender hardware address> to its translation table.

normative.quote: ?Is the opcode ares_op$REQUEST?
normative.obligation: The receiver must test whether ar$op is ares_op$REQUEST, and generate a reply only if it is.

normative.quote: (NOW look at the opcode!!)
normative.obligation: The receiver must not look at the opcode until after the table merge and add steps have been performed.

normative.quote: Swap hardware and protocol fields, putting the local hardware and protocol addresses in the sender fields.
normative.obligation: To answer a request the receiver must swap the hardware and protocol address fields so that its own hardware and protocol addresses occupy the sender fields and the requester's occupy the target fields.

normative.quote: Set the ar$op field to ares_op$REPLY
normative.obligation: In the answering packet the receiver must set ar$op to ares_op$REPLY.

normative.quote: Send the packet to the (new) target hardware address
normative.obligation: The receiver must send the reply to the new target hardware address, that is, directly to the requester rather than by broadcast.

normative.quote: on the same hardware on which the request was received
normative.obligation: The receiver must send the reply out on the same hardware on which the request arrived.

normative.quote: Notice also that if an entry already exists for the <protocol type, sender protocol address> pair, then the new hardware address supersedes the old one.
normative.obligation: A newly received sender hardware address must supersede the hardware address already stored for the same <protocol type, sender protocol address> pair.

normative.quote: The ar$hrd and ar$hln fields allow this protocol and packet format to be used for non-10Mbit Ethernets.
normative.obligation: The ar$hrd and ar$hln fields must carry the hardware type and hardware address length so that the same protocol and packet format work on hardware other than 10Mbit Ethernet.

normative.quote: For the 10Mbit Ethernet <ar$hrd, ar$hln> takes on the value <1, 6>.
normative.obligation: On 10Mbit Ethernet the pair <ar$hrd, ar$hln> must be <1, 6>.

normative.quote: For other hardware networks, the ar$pro field may no longer correspond to the Ethernet type field
normative.obligation: On hardware other than Ethernet an implementation must not assume ar$pro is an Ethernet type field value.

normative.quote: it should be associated with the protocol whose address resolution is being sought
normative.obligation: On non-Ethernet hardware the ar$pro value should identify the protocol whose address resolution is being sought.

normative.section: Why is it done this way??
normative.quote: Periodic broadcasting is definitely not desired.
normative.obligation: An implementation must not distribute address resolution information by periodic broadcast.

normative.section: Why is it done this way??
normative.quote: This format does not allow for more than one resolution to be done in the same packet.
normative.obligation: An implementation must carry at most one address resolution per packet; the format admits no multiplexing of several resolutions.

normative.section: Why is it done this way??
normative.quote: a reply has the same length as a request, and several of the fields are the same
normative.obligation: A reply must have the same length as the request that provoked it, with several fields carried over unchanged.

normative.section: Why is it done this way??
normative.quote: The value of the hardware field (ar$hrd) is taken from a list for this purpose.  Currently the only defined value is for the 10Mbit Ethernet (ares_hrd$Ethernet = 1).
normative.obligation: An implementation must take ar$hrd values from the assigned hardware-type list, of which 1 (10Mbit Ethernet) is the only value defined by this document.

normative.section: Why is it done this way??
normative.quote: the length fields (ar$hln and ar$pln) are redundant, since the length of a protocol address should be determined by the hardware type (found in ar$hrd) and the protocol type (found in ar$pro)
normative.obligation: An implementation should determine hardware and protocol address lengths from the hardware type in ar$hrd and the protocol type in ar$pro rather than from the length fields alone.

normative.section: Why is it done this way??
normative.quote: if one assumes a reply is only provoked by a request
normative.obligation: A reply is sent only in response to a request; an implementation does not emit unprovoked replies.

normative.section: Why is it done this way??
normative.quote: It has no meaning in the request form, since it is this number that the machine is requesting.
normative.obligation: A receiver must not attach meaning to ar$tha in a packet whose opcode is a request.

normative.section: Why is it done this way??
normative.quote: Its meaning in the reply form is the address of the machine making the request.
normative.obligation: In a reply, ar$tha holds the hardware address of the machine that made the request.

normative.section: Why is it done this way??
normative.quote: There are no padding bytes between addresses.
normative.obligation: An implementation must emit the address fields contiguously, inserting no padding bytes between them.

normative.section: Why is it done this way??
normative.quote: The packet data should be viewed as a byte stream in which only 3 byte pairs are defined to be words (ar$hrd, ar$pro and ar$op)
normative.obligation: An implementation should treat the packet data as a byte stream in which only ar$hrd, ar$pro and ar$op are words, all other fields being byte sequences.

normative.section: Why is it done this way??
normative.quote: which are sent most significant byte first (Ethernet/PDP-10 byte style)
normative.obligation: The three word fields ar$hrd, ar$pro and ar$op must be sent most significant byte first.

normative.quote: When a monitor receives an Address Resolution packet, it always enters the <protocol type, sender protocol address, sender hardware address> in a table.
normative.obligation: A node acting as a monitor enters the <protocol type, sender protocol address, sender hardware address> triplet in its table for every address resolution packet received, without applying the target-address gate of the reception algorithm.

normative.quote: It may be desirable to have table aging and/or timeouts.
normative.obligation: An implementation may age out or time out translation table entries.

normative.quote: If a host moves, any connections initiated by that host will work, assuming its own address resolution table is cleared when it moves.
normative.obligation: A host that moves clears its own address resolution table.

normative.quote: 48.bit Ethernet addresses are supposed to be unique and fixed for all time, so they shouldn't change.
normative.obligation: The protocol relies on 48-bit Ethernet addresses being unique and permanently fixed to a piece of hardware.

normative.quote: it should not be allowed to persist forever
normative.obligation: An implementation should not allow incorrect translation information to persist in the table forever.

normative.quote: Perhaps failure to initiate a connection should inform the Address Resolution module to delete the information on the basis that the host is not reachable, possibly because it is down or the old translation is no longer valid.
normative.obligation: On failure to initiate a connection, the Address Resolution module should perhaps be told to delete the translation entry for the unreachable host.

normative.quote: Or perhaps receiving of a packet from a host should reset a timeout in the address resolution entry used for transmitting packets to that host
normative.obligation: Receipt of a packet from a host should perhaps reset the timeout on the translation entry used to transmit to that host.

normative.quote: if no packets are received from a host for a suitable length of time, the address resolution entry is forgotten
normative.obligation: A translation entry is forgotten when no packet has been received from that host for a suitable length of time.

normative.quote: on a perfect Ethernet where a broadcast REQUEST reaches all stations on the cable, each station will be get the new hardware address
normative.obligation: Where a broadcast request reaches every station, every station that holds an entry for the sender must end up holding the sender's new hardware address.

normative.quote: Another alternative is to have a daemon perform the timeouts.  After a suitable time, the daemon considers removing an entry.
normative.obligation: Timeouts may instead be performed by a daemon that considers an entry for removal after a suitable time.

normative.quote: It first sends (with a small number of retransmissions if needed) an address resolution packet with opcode REQUEST directly to the Ethernet address in the table.
normative.obligation: Before removing an entry the daemon first sends a REQUEST packet, with a small number of retransmissions if needed, directly to the Ethernet address recorded in that entry rather than by broadcast.

normative.quote: If a REPLY is not seen in a short amount of time, the entry is deleted.
normative.obligation: If no REPLY arrives within a short time of the daemon's probe, the entry is deleted.

normative.quote: Since hosts don't transmit information about anyone other than themselves
normative.obligation: A host transmits address resolution information only about itself, never about another host.

normative.quote: Perhaps manually resetting (or clearing) the address mapping table will suffice.
normative.obligation: An implementation may perhaps provide manual resetting or clearing of the address mapping table as the remedy for stale entries.
